Subject: Post-call: hosted feasibility, SLO targets, and onramp checklist

Hi Alyssa —

Thanks again for your time this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment before the sandbox:

Key takeaways from our demo
- Primary use: customer support assistant (conversational flows) + lightweight product recommendation embedding lookups.
- Latency sensitivity: P95 matters for UX, especially during promotional spikes. You called out a target of p95 ~300ms if possible.
- Data residency/compliance: BrightMap prefers hosted for trial but may require private/VPC for production if any regulated data is in scope.

Open questions we flagged
1) Expected steady-state and burst RPS (per endpoint): please confirm (I remember ~120–180 steady, up to ~350 burst).
2) Avg/peak prompt + response token sizes (we estimated ~120 in / ~40 out).
3) Any hard SLA expectations (uptime/SLO) for the proof-of-concept?

What Redwood can provision for the hosted eval
- Sandbox endpoints mapped to 3 routes (chat, embeddings, rerank). Each route can have independent rate caps and token ceilings.
- Prefix/KV caching to reduce token consumption for repeated queries, and autoscaling within the reserved trial envelope.
- Canary rollout guidance: we can route a % of traffic to a lower-cost model if you want a graceful fallback for spikes.

Attachments: I included a short demo recording and a one-pager summarizing the endpoints & recommended rate ceilings for the trial.

Proposed next actions (owners + timing)
- Alyssa: confirm RPS & token sizes by Friday (11/20).
- Jordan (SE): allocate a sandbox with endpoint mapping and proposed rate caps by Mon 11/22.
- Monica (CS): set up onboarding session and add your legal contact to the security questionnaire thread.

If that sounds good I’ll drop a calendar for a quick sandbox kick-off next week.

Thanks —
Ben

Ben —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming a few items from our side:

Traffic profile
- Steady-state: ~150 RPS across the combined chat + recommendation endpoints.
- Promotional spikes: up to ~350 RPS for short windows (5–10 minutes), historically once per day during campaigns.

Payloads
- Average prompt length: ~100–140 tokens.
- Average response length: ~30–60 tokens.

SLOs & risk
- For the proof-of-concept we need p95 <= 400ms for chat to keep product team happy. Production SLA TBD — likely 99.9% uptime target if we proceed to Dedicated/Private.
- Data residency: BrightMap is not subject to HIPAA, but we do store some payment metadata and PII. For now the hosted eval is fine; we’ll surface stricter controls if legal flags anything.

Asks from BrightMap
1) Can you provision a sandbox with three endpoints and the rate caps you proposed? We want the ability to independently throttle chat vs embedding requests.
2) Cost estimate for the trial (2 weeks of sandbox traffic at steady-state + 2 promotional spikes).
3) Sample security questionnaire (Tom will own legal/security review).

Tom Reyes (cc) will be our legal/infosec point for the questionnaire.

Thanks — I’ll aim to get the RPS confirmation and any compliance flags by Thursday EOD.

—Alyssa

Hi Alyssa / Ben —

Technical follow-up from my side with concrete sandbox plan and conservative estimates:

Recommended sandbox topology
- Endpoints: /chat, /embed, /rerank. Each endpoint gets an independent token budget + rate cap.
- Instance sizing: for your steady-state (~150 RPS) we recommend a pool that sustains ~200 RPS with headroom for short bursts if you allow autoscale (can add burst nodes for the promo windows).
- Model variant: suggest using Redwood-llama-13b-q4 (good balance of latency/cost). For baseline p95 ~200–350ms on NVIDIA H100-class hardware for typical token lengths; p99 will be higher during spikes.

Rate limiting & SLO
- We'll propose per-endpoint caps: chat 200 RPS steady / 400 RPS burst ceiling; embed 60 RPS steady / 120 burst; rerank 30 RPS steady. These are configurable in the sandbox.
- Caching: enable prefix caching on chat for repeated prompts and KV cache reuse for multipart conversations — expect 10–30% token reduction depending on session patterns.

Fallbacks and rollout
- Canary plan: route 5–10% traffic to a lower-cost quantized variant for the first 48 hours of the trial, increase if metrics look good.
- Fallback route: automatic model variant fallback under sustained queueing to keep latency within the p95 target (we'll surface monitoring alerts).

Deliverables we’ll provide (by Mon 11/22)
- Sandbox with 3 endpoints + the rate caps above.
- A small runbook describing how to flip canary %s and view per-route telemetry.
- A simple cost estimate for 2-week trial at steady-state + spikes.

I attached an endpoint matrix (spreadsheet) with the initial caps and token ceilings. Please flag anything that looks off and I’ll adjust before provisioning.

Jordan Blake
